hints.mmDLydDom: D Lydian dominant (from A melodic minor)
hints.hmPhrygianDom: E Phrygian dominant (from A harmonic minor)
hints.mixolydianF: F is the bVII chord — stay in G mixolydian
hints.lickBluesAnswer: Lick: the answer with a bend
hints.boxRoot: Around the root on the B string (fret 10)
hints.triadPairFG: F (F A C) + G (G B D)

lick.transposed: The lick description refers to the original key ({{key}}).
lick.notes: Notes of the lick in order
lick.legend: Numbers are the order of the notes. A position with several numbers is played several times. Standard tuning.
lick.legendTech: Marks next to the notes: ¼↑, ½↑, 1↑ — bend by a quarter tone, a half step, a whole step; h — hammer-on, p — pull-off, s — slide from the previous note, ~ — vibrato; + — two notes together.

pent3Descent.name: Down through the box
pent3Descent.tip: Down the box from the top note to the root A. End calmly, on a longer note.

pent3Answer.name: Question and answer
pent3Answer.tip: The first half climbs and hangs on G, the second returns to A. Leave a short pause between them.

pent3Blue.name: With the blue note
pent3Blue.tip: Adds Eb (fret 8 on the G string) between D and E. Pass through it quickly, do not stop on it.

pos6Climb.name: From box 1 to box 2
pos6Climb.tip: Climbs from the first box into the second and ends on G.

pos6Slide.name: Along the B string
pos6Slide.tip: The whole phrase on the B string: D, F, G and back. It shows the scale horizontally.

arp11Am7.name: Am7 arpeggio up and down
arp11Am7.tip: A, C, E, G and back. Chord tones only, so every note sounds sure.

arp11Cmaj7.name: Cmaj7 arpeggio
arp11Cmaj7.tip: C, E, G, B and C an octave up. The major seventh (B) gives the colour.

arp11TwoFiveOne.name: ii–V–I in arpeggios
arp11TwoFiveOne.tip: Four notes each from Dm7, G7 and Cmaj7. The phrase ends on B, the seventh of Cmaj7.

tgt12Am.name: Landing on C over Am
tgt12Am.tip: The phrase circles E and D and ends on C, the third of Am.

tgt12C.name: Landing on E over C
tgt12C.tip: The same idea over C: it ends on E, the third of C.

bluesBoogie.name: The boogie riff
bluesBoogie.tip: The open A string with the fifth (fret 2 on the D string), then with the sixth (fret 4). Mute the strings with your palm at the bridge.

bluesBoogieSeventh.name: Boogie riff with the seventh
bluesBoogieSeventh.tip: The same riff, but in the second half of the bar the finger reaches for the seventh (fret 5) and comes back to the sixth.

bluesBendFifth.name: Bend to the fifth
bluesBendFifth.tip: Bend D up to E, answer with two notes and end on the root A with vibrato.

bluesBendRoot.name: Bend to the root
bluesBendRoot.tip: Bend G up to A and come down through the box to the lower root. Hold the first note long.

bluesCurl.name: The third with a curl
bluesCurl.tip: C nudged up, then straight to the root A. The third should sound between C and C#.

bluesOpen.name: The opener
bluesOpen.tip: A short phrase to start a chorus. Hammer on the second note and end on the root.

bluesTriplet.name: Triplets
bluesTriplet.tip: Three notes repeated in triplets. Keep them even and end on the high root.

bluesBlueNote.name: With the blue note
bluesBlueNote.tip: A run down the box with Eb as a passing note between E and D.

bluesSlide.name: Slide into box 2
bluesSlide.tip: Two slides move the hand from box 1 to box 2. End on the root with vibrato.

bluesAnswer.name: The answer
bluesAnswer.tip: It starts with a bend to the fifth and comes calmly down to the root. A good answer to any phrase.

bluesLow.name: On the bass strings
bluesLow.tip: The same scale on the three lowest strings, with the blue note on the way.

bluesBoxCall.name: Root and a bend
bluesBoxCall.tip: The root A on the B string, then B bent up to C# and back to the root with vibrato.

bluesBoxSweet.name: The sixth and a half step
bluesBoxSweet.tip: It starts on the sixth (F#). Bend the second only a half step, to the minor third.

bluesTurnDown.name: Turnaround going down
bluesTurnDown.tip: The line G–F#–F–E on the D string alternating with the high A. It ends on E, the root of the V chord.

bluesTurnUp.name: Turnaround going up
bluesTurnUp.tip: From A on the low E string (fret 5) chromatically up to E on the A string: C#, D, D#, E.

triadArpC.name: C major arpeggio
triadArpC.tip: The C major triad up and down on strings 1-2-3, through two inversions.

triadChanges.name: Following C–Am–F–G
triadChanges.tip: The three notes of each chord in turn; between chords the hand moves two frets at most.

pairFG.name: F and G going up
pairFG.tip: First the F triad, then G a whole step higher, ending on A.

pairFGDown.name: F and G going down
pairFGDown.tip: The same six notes from D downwards, ending on A.

review.name: Review: mixed quiz
review.desc: 10 questions from modules you have passed. Topics you have not reviewed for a while, or got wrong, come back first.
review.disabledHint: Available after you pass your first module.

improv.title: Improvisation
improv.description: Learn guitar improvisation in 22 graded modules, from the E-string notes to Giant Steps. Each module pairs a short theory recap with exercises; passing them unlocks the next module.
improv.promise: Freedom to improvise: from the notes on the neck through scales and arpeggios to playing over chord changes.
improv.duration: About 4–6 months at 20 minutes a day

blues.title: Blues
blues.description: Learn the blues in 14 modules: from the 12-bar form and the shuffle, through bends and phrasing, to playing the changes.
blues.promise: Play your first solo over a 12-bar blues: shuffle, bends, phrasing and playing the changes.
blues.duration: About 2–3 months at 15 minutes a day

voicings.title: Triads and voice leading
voicings.description: Learn triads in 12 modules: inversions on every string set, the whole fretboard map, voice leading through real progressions, and triads in your solos.
voicings.promise: Play any chord anywhere on the neck and move between chords without jumping around.
voicings.duration: About 6–8 weeks at 15 minutes a day

sevenths.title: Seventh chords and comping
sevenths.description: Learn seventh chords in 12 modules: shell voicings, drop 2 and drop 3 voicings, guide tones, and comping real progressions.
sevenths.promise: Comp in jazz, soul and bossa: from three strings to full drop 2 voicings.
sevenths.duration: About 2–3 months at 20 minutes a day

ear.title: Ear training for guitarists
ear.description: Ear training in 12 modules: scale degrees after a cadence, intervals, chord qualities and inversions, chord functions and progressions, then playing by ear.
ear.promise: Recognise degrees, intervals and chords, then play back by ear what you hear.
ear.duration: About 2–3 months at 15 minutes a day

prompt.half: String {{string}}, fret {{fret}} ({{note}}): bend up a half step, to {{target}}.
prompt.whole: String {{string}}, fret {{fret}} ({{note}}): bend up a whole step, to {{target}}.
prompt.curl: String {{string}}, fret {{fret}} ({{note}}): bend slightly, by a quarter tone. The note should stay below {{target}}.

bend.micOffHint: Turn the microphone on to see how far you bend. The green area is the target.
bend.waiting: Play the note and bend the string.
bend.holdHint: A repetition counts when you hold the note in the green area for {{seconds}} s. Release the string before the next one.

voicing.legend: Numbers are chord degrees. Green: the note stays in the next chord. Arrow: the direction the voice will move. Faded: the next voicing.
voicing.empty: This chord has no voicing on this string set.
voicing.runNeedsMetronome: First go through every voicing with the metronome ({{steps}}).

echo.promptMajor: Key of {{key}} major. Listen to the cadence and the notes after it, then play them on the guitar in any octave.
echo.promptMinor: Key of {{key}} minor. Listen to the cadence and the notes after it, then play them on the guitar in any octave.
echo.micOffHint: Turn on the microphone so the app can check what you play. Without it, mark the phrase yourself.
echo.waiting: Play the phrase. A wrong note starts the attempt over.

learn.title: Learning paths
learn.description: Pick a goal and go step by step. Each path leads through short modules with theory, exercises and backing tracks, and the app remembers where you stopped.
